data.why: A small plane stands on a concrete runway on the lawn and is built up in the order the problems demand: wings, engine and propeller, curved wing, tail, hinged tail surfaces. Counters on poles show its weight and speed. The takeoff is one rig move, so the mechanism reads in a single wide shot. Gust, landing and the engine myth follow, and the finish adds a door, windows and boarding stairs.

ideas.idea: bolt two wings onto a tube and you think you have an airplane
flat wings give no lift, so the plane just sits on the runway
it weighs about 1100 kilograms and gravity pins every kilogram down
an engine and propeller push air past the wings, but a flat wing just lets it slide by
curve the top of the wing so air speeds up over it and the wing is pushed up
a tail with a fin and stabilizer keeps the nose pointing straight
hinge the back of the tail so the rudder and elevator can swing the nose sideways and up
this whole machine is an airplane
the curved wing shape has its own name, an airfoil
at about 100 kilometers per hour the air over the wings lifts the plane off the runway
a gust of wind pushes one wing down and the plane rolls onto its side
to land it must slow down, but at 100 kilometers per hour it is far too fast
flaps on the wings level the plane and slow it so it settles onto the runway
the engine is not what holds a plane up
the wing does the lifting, so with the engine off a small plane glides nine meters forward for every meter it drops
add a door, windows and stairs so people can board
the finished airplane stands calm on the runway

chain.stakes: a plane that never leaves the ground, 1100 kg pinned down

chain.shows: a gust arrow pushes down one wing and the plane tips onto its side in the air
chain.stakes: a plane rolling over high above the runway

chain.shows: the speed gauge climbs and turns red while the plane is still in the air
chain.stakes: a plane that cannot slow down to touch down on the runway

surprises.claim: A Cessna 172 has a maximum takeoff weight of about 1,111 kg (2,450 lb)
A Cessna 172 lifts off at about 55 knots, roughly 100 km/h
A Cessna 172 has about 16 square meters (174 sq ft) of wing, so each square meter carries roughly 70 kg at takeoff
A Cessna 172 with the engine off glides about 9 meters forward for every meter it drops
